### Summary

This appendix is the index that the chapters cite for an environment variable: one row per variable, with the
function that reads it at the pin, its default, its effect and the chapters that use it. @sec-ch12 owns the
treatment: the parsing rules in @sec-ch12-environment, the launch variables in @sec-ch12-layout and the switch
combinations in @sec-ch12-matrix. Variables that only snapy's tests read are in @sec-ch12-test-environment and are
not repeated here.

::: {.callout-note title="At a glance"}
**Purpose.** Index of every environment variable snapy reads or sets at the pin, for the chapters to cite.

**Data.** 17 variables in four groups: 1 numerics switch, 11 launch and process-group variables, 3 UCX defaults,
2 build variables.

**Placement.** The numerics switch: the first call of its accessor. Launch: each construction of layout options.
The Gloo interface: process-group construction.

**Activation.** `SNAP_X1_CENTROID_EXACT` is off unless set; the launch variables default to one process on the CPU.

**Guarantee / limits.** The switch is read once per process; nothing checks that ranks agree.

**Evidence.** The ctest arms of @tbl-appd-tests; full treatment in @sec-ch12-environment.
:::

One numerics switch is read from the environment at the pin, `SNAP_X1_CENTROID_EXACT`: on a spherical-polar grid it
makes the reconstruction, the $x_1$ pressure source and the scalar's radial table read plain means instead of
$r^2$-weighted cell averages (@sec-ch12-centroid). It is an environment variable and not a deck key because every
block of a process must make the same choice, or the two sides of an $x_1$ seam stop agreeing; the accessor's own
comment says so ({{< code src/coord/x1_centroid.cpp x1_centroid_exact_enabled >}}).

The other numerics choices a reader may look for here are deck keys, listed in @tbl-appd-keys and in @sec-appi:
the lateral face-flux covariance (`dynamics/flux-covariance`, on by default), the radial velocity mean correction
(`dynamics/x1-mass-covariance`, off by default) and the fourth-order cell-consistent reference
(`dynamics/conversion-order: 4`). The corrected potential-energy face work has no switch at all: it follows from
`gravity-work: face`, the one accepted value, with nonzero `grav1` on a grid that has an $x_1$ measure
({{< code src/hydro/hydro.cpp HydroImpl::radial_exact_work >}}).

The scope is `src/`, `python/` and `setup.py` at the pin. Variables read by kintera, pyharp, commux, PyTorch, Gloo
or UCX themselves are not listed, except the one Gloo variable snapy reads on their behalf,
`GLOO_SOCKET_IFNAME`.

### Derivation

None: the switch selects a scheme whose derivation is in @sec-ch12-centroid and @sec-ch03; the launch variables
select no numerics.

### Numerical method

The numerics switch is decided once per process, in five steps fixed by its accessor
({{< code src/coord/x1_centroid.cpp x1_centroid_exact_enabled >}}):

1. *Read.* `get_env` returns the variable's value when it is set, the empty string included, and the accessor's
   default `"0"` only when it is absent ({{< code src/layout/layout.hpp get_env >}}).
2. *Normalise.* The value is lower-cased; it is not trimmed, so `false ` with a trailing space is a value of its own.
3. *Decide.* The switch is off when the value is empty, `0`, `false`, `off` or `no`. Every other value is on.
4. *Cache.* The result is kept in a function-local `static`, so the first call fixes it for every block of the
   process, and a later change of the environment has no effect.
5. *Act.* Four sites read the cached value. The coordinate's $x_1$ row faces take the plain-mean branch on a
   spherical-polar grid ({{< code src/coord/coordinate.cpp CoordinateImpl::x1_row_faces >}}); the spherical-polar
   forward builds the $x_1$ pressure-source stencils when face pressures are defined
   ({{< code src/coord/spherical_polar.cpp SphericalPolarImpl::forward >}}); the hydro forward converts the
   primitives of a spherical-polar block to plain means before the reconstruction
   ({{< code src/hydro/hydro_forward.cpp HydroImpl::forward >}}); and the balance of a rest column refuses any
   geometry but Cartesian ({{< code src/hydro/balance_column.cpp balance_column >}}). On a Cartesian or
   gnomonic-equiangle grid the first three sites do nothing.

The switch shares one requirement with `dynamics/conversion-order: 4`: both read scan pressures three cells away,
so with nonzero `grav1` the block needs `nghost` of at least 3, checked at setup
({{< code src/hydro/hydro.cpp HydroImpl::reset >}}).

The launch variables are read each time layout options are constructed
({{< code src/layout/layout.cpp LayoutOptionsImpl::LayoutOptionsImpl >}}). The `BACKEND` default comes from
`default_backend` ({{< code src/layout/layout.cpp default_backend >}}): `ucx` in a build with UCX, except on macOS,
else `gloo`. The deck's `distribute/backend` key is accepted and ignored, and there is no deck key for the device;
both rows of the options schema say so ({{< code src/options/layout.yaml >}}). A Gloo process group reads
`GLOO_SOCKET_IFNAME` once, when it is constructed, and binds its device to that interface instead of resolving the
host ({{< code src/layout/process_group.cpp ProcessGroupContext::_init_gloo >}}). The three communication defaults
are written, not read, by `set_default_env` ({{< code src/layout/process_group_ucx.cpp set_default_env >}}), only
when the variable is unset and only in a build with UCX, as the UCX process group starts
({{< code src/layout/process_group_ucx.cpp ProcessGroupContext::_init_ucx >}}); they are listed because they change
the process environment that commux sees.

### Code

**How to set the switch.** It is an environment variable of the process that runs snapy, set before it starts;
there is no YAML key for it. For example, the Straka deck in `build/bin` of a build at the pin
([Install and run](#sec-preface-install)):

```sh
SNAP_X1_CENTROID_EXACT=1 ./straka.release straka_single.yaml
```

The deck is Cartesian, so the switch changes no number of that run; it only adds the `nghost` requirement of
refusal 1 below, which the deck's `nghost: 3` meets. A run with several processes needs a common rendezvous port,
which `torchrun` sets from `--master-port`:
`torchrun --no-python --nproc-per-node=2 --master-port=29573 ./straka.release straka_proc2.yaml`.

**What is refused, and why.** Nothing in the parse refuses a value: an unrecognised value turns the switch on
(step 3 of the Numerical method above). Setup refuses four combinations:

1. *`SNAP_X1_CENTROID_EXACT` (or `dynamics/conversion-order: 4`) with nonzero `grav1` and `nghost` below 3*: the
   resolution flag reads scan pressures three cells away, so both sides of an $x_1$ seam agree only with three
   ghost cells ({{< code src/hydro/hydro.cpp HydroImpl::reset >}}).
2. *`SNAP_X1_CENTROID_EXACT` with a rest column whose geometry is not `cartesian`*: `balance_column` does no
   $r^2$-to-plain-mean conversion, so a spherical-polar column's rest state is left to the solver's own reference
   ({{< code src/hydro/balance_column.cpp balance_column >}}).
3. *An unset `MASTER_PORT` with either world size above 1*: the processes could not meet on one store
   ({{< code src/layout/layout.cpp LayoutOptionsImpl::LayoutOptionsImpl >}}).
4. *`GLOO_SOCKET_IFNAME` naming an interface the host does not have*: the Gloo device is created for that interface
   and the process group fails to start on every rank with `Unable to find address for: <name>`
   ({{< code src/layout/process_group.cpp ProcessGroupContext::_init_gloo >}}); `test_gloo_invalid_interface` in
   @tbl-appd-tests expects exactly that failure on both ranks.

**The code, mapped to the five steps of the Numerical method above**
({{< code src/coord/x1_centroid.cpp x1_centroid_exact_enabled >}}):

```cpp
bool x1_centroid_exact_enabled() {
  static const bool on = [] {                                    // step 4: once per process
    auto v = get_env("SNAP_X1_CENTROID_EXACT", "0");             // step 1: default "0" only if unset
    std::transform(v.begin(), v.end(), v.begin(),
                   [](unsigned char c) { return std::tolower(c); });   // step 2: lower-case, no trim
    return !(v.empty() || v == "0" || v == "false" || v == "off" || v == "no");  // step 3
  }();
  return on;                                                     // step 5: read at four sites
}
```

### Tests

The ctest registrations set the switch and the backend per entry ({{< code tests/CMakeLists.txt >}}). Each row is
one variable; the test names are the registered ctest names, without the build-type suffix. The seam arms pass
only on gtest's own line `[  PASSED  ] 1 test.`, so a skipped or empty arm fails its entry.

| test (ctest name) | what it asserts | tolerance | where the tolerance comes from |
|---|---|---|---|
| `test_x1_seam_split_x1_centroid`, `test_x1_seam_split_mp_x1_centroid` (two ranks), `test_x1_seam_split_x1_centroid_cuda` (CUDA builds) | with `SNAP_X1_CENTROID_EXACT=1` the split column equals one block, across the seam and across two ranks | exact: one gtest pass line | the test registration |
| `test_x1_seam_split_nghost_check_x1_centroid` | with `SNAP_X1_CENTROID_EXACT=1` and gravity, a block with fewer than 3 ghost cells is refused (refusal 1) | exact: throws | a guard |
| `test_deck_x1_wiring_x1_centroid` | with `SNAP_X1_CENTROID_EXACT=1` the scalar keeps the $r^3/3$ table of a spherical-polar deck while the hydro reads plain means | per test | the test source |
| `test_stretched_x1_ref_x1_centroid` | with `SNAP_X1_CENTROID_EXACT=1` the stretched $x_1$ reference and the balance of a Cartesian column still run | per test | the test source |
| `test_balance_column_x1_centroid`, `test_face_floor_x1_centroid` | with `SNAP_X1_CENTROID_EXACT=1` the same balance and floor checks hold on their Cartesian columns | per test | the test sources |
| `test_diffusion_cubed_sphere_mp`, `test_conservation_budget_mp` (three ranks), `test_parentless_cloud_nb1_mp_gloo` (UCX builds) | `BACKEND=gloo`: the two- and three-rank cases on Gloo, which a UCX build would not reach by default | per test | the test sources |
| `test_gloo_invalid_interface` | `BACKEND=gloo` with `GLOO_SOCKET_IFNAME=snapy_no_such_interface`: the two-rank launch fails instead of resolving the host (refusal 4) | exact: expected failure | the wrapper script of the registration |
| `test_exchange_ucx` (UCX builds) | `BACKEND=ucx` with the exchange topology variables of @sec-ch12-test-environment | per test | the test source |
| `test_diffusion_cubed_sphere_two_gpu_ucx` (CUDA and commux-CUDA builds) | `BACKEND=ucx`, `DEVICE=cuda` and an explicit `UCX_TLS=self,tcp,cuda_copy,cuda_ipc`, which the set-if-unset default of @tbl-appd-layout leaves alone | per test | the test source |

: Ctest entries that set an environment variable of this appendix, at the pin. {#tbl-appd-tests}

The registered names and their assertions are in @sec-appc. No check script of this report covers this appendix.
The entries of @tbl-appd-tests that a CPU build registers were run at the pin for it[^appd-run]: ten of the eleven
passed, and `test_gloo_invalid_interface` failed for a reason that is not the interface check. Its binary compiles
its one test only with `NETCDFOUTPUT` ({{< code tests/test_output_barrier.cpp >}}), so in a build without NetCDF
both ranks run zero tests and exit 0, and the wrapper stops with `expected two interface errors; exit=0,
matches=0`. In a build with NetCDF (`-DNETCDF=ON -DPNETCDF=ON`, same tree, same host) the entry passes, with
`test_output_barrier` itself. The CUDA and UCX-on-GPU arms were not run.

[^appd-run]: `ctest -j 1` on the entries by name, in a Release build at the pin configured with `cmake -DCUDA=OFF
    -DNETCDF=OFF -DPNETCDF=OFF -DUCX=ON`, kintera 2.6.13, pyharp 2.7.17, torch 2.10.0+cu128, Linux x86-64, the
    multi-rank entries as two or three `torchrun` ranks on one host. Passed: `test_x1_seam_split_x1_centroid`,
    `test_x1_seam_split_nghost_check_x1_centroid`, `test_x1_seam_split_mp_x1_centroid`,
    `test_deck_x1_wiring_x1_centroid`, `test_stretched_x1_ref_x1_centroid`, `test_balance_column_x1_centroid`,
    `test_face_floor_x1_centroid`, `test_diffusion_cubed_sphere_mp`, `test_conservation_budget_mp`,
    `test_parentless_cloud_nb1_mp_gloo`, `test_exchange_ucx`. Failed: `test_gloo_invalid_interface`, as described.
    One run, one host.

### Limits

::: {.callout-warning title="Limits"}
A switch that differs between ranks makes shared faces two-valued, and no code compares the ranks' values.
The switch changed after the first call has no effect in that process.
:::

- `distribute/backend` in YAML is accepted and ignored; only `BACKEND` selects the backend.
- `LOCAL_RANK` has two defaults: 0 in the C++ layout options, the rank modulo the GPU count in `init_dist`.
- An unset `NC_HOME` adds the literal path `None/lib` to the package build's library path.
- The scope is `src/`, `python/` and `setup.py` at the pin; environment variables read by kintera, pyharp, commux,
  PyTorch, Gloo or UCX themselves are not listed, apart from `GLOO_SOCKET_IFNAME`, which snapy reads itself.
- The CUDA and UCX arms of @tbl-appd-tests register only in a build with that option; the evidence above is a CPU
  build without CUDA, so those arms are not run here.
